title: Speech Tokenizers and Speech Language Models: A Survey of Representations, Modeling, and Systems

sections.description: Motivate the shift from cascaded ASR→LLM→TTS to unified Speech Language Models (SLMs), set scope across tokenizers/codecs, encoders, decoders, language modeling, training, systems, datasets, evaluation, efficiency, and safety, and state contributions and boundaries.

subsections.subsection title: Why now: From cascaded pipelines to unified end-to-end Speech Language Models
subsections.description: Explain technical catalysts (scaling, neural codecs, self-supervised encoders, modality projectors) and user needs (interactive agents, duplex dialogue) that make end-to-end SLMs timely.

Define included topics (token types and rates; modeling and generation; alignment and evaluation) and contributions: token taxonomy, comparative design analysis, and unified training/evaluation practices.
Introduce the core tension among semantic fidelity, acoustic detail, and latency/bitrate, framing trade-offs addressed throughout the survey.

Provide 1–2 sentence previews of Sections 2–17 to orient readers to background, tokenization, encoders, decoding, modeling, training, systems, expressivity, streaming, datasets, metrics, efficiency, safety, tools, challenges, and conclusions.
State exclusions (e.g., purely text-only LLMs, classic HMM/GMM pipelines, non-speech audio tasks unless informative) and limit depth on peripheral modalities.

sections.description: Establish the end-to-end pipeline and terminology spanning waveform→representations→tokens→LM→audio, and situate canonical components, datasets, and evaluation families.

subsections.subsection title: From waveform to language model and back: pipeline and terminology
subsections.description: Define speech tokenizer/quantizer, neural audio codec, VQ/RVQ, discrete vs continuous tokens, semantic/acoustic/paralinguistic/mixed tokens, encoders, token-to-speech decoders, vocoders.
Briefly summarize representative models across the stack (Encodec, SoundStream, HiFi-GAN, HuBERT, wav2vec, data2vec, Whisper, PAST) and their roles.
Clarify semantic vs acoustic vs paralinguistic vs mixed vs continuous interfaces, typical bitrates and sequence lengths, and implications for LM context.

subsections.subsection title: Datasets and evaluation families: a primer
subsections.description: Give a compact overview of core corpora (LibriSpeech, Common Voice, VoxPopuli, LibriTTS, CoVoST2, VoxCeleb, GigaSpeech, AISHELL, Fisher) and evaluation families (ABX, sWUGGY/sBLIMP, sStoryCloze, SUPERB, VoxEval, MOS, WER, BLEU, BERTScore, FAD, RTF).

sections.section title: Speech Tokenization and Neural Audio Codecs
sections.description: Survey methods that map audio to discrete units or compact vectors, emphasizing objectives, quantization, rate control, and design trade-offs.

subsections.subsection title: Tokenization objectives and interfaces: the LM-facing contract
subsections.description: Specify objectives (reconstruction, semantic preservation, prosody retention) and how token streams interface with LMs in terms of predictability and conditioning.
Detail VQ/RVQ, residual/product quantization, RQ-Transformer, PQ-VAE, FSQ/BSQ; discuss index collapse prevention, codebook usage, and stability.

subsections.subsection title: From continuous features to units: discretization and codebook design
subsections.description: Cover discretization sources (encoder layers), granularity, codebook size/coarseness, and their effects on phone/word/sentence tasks.
Discuss frame-rate selection, bitrate/sequence-length trade-offs, acoustic BPE, compression, and robustness under low-bitrate constraints.
Explain multi-stream/hybrid tokens separating semantics, acoustics, and prosody; mechanisms for style/content disentanglement.
Examine continuous token/feature interfaces, codec-free models, and their robustness/latency properties versus discrete units.
Compare Encodec, SoundStream, PAST, ALMTokenizer, RepCodec, HASRD, XY Tokenizer, LM-SPT, Universal token learning; summarize bitrate, reconstruction, semantic alignment.

subsections.subsection title: Comparative evaluation axes and open issues
subsections.description: Lay out axes (reconstruction, bitrate, sequence length, semantic fidelity, downstream SLM performance, cross-language transfer) and open challenges.

sections.description: Review encoder families, representation properties, and their use or discretization for downstream SLMs.

subsections.description: Survey HuBERT, wav2vec, data2vec, Whisper, PAST; discuss layer-wise phonetic/semantic specialization and selection.
Describe fusion across layers/models and heuristics for choosing layers for tokenization or direct conditioning.
Analyze noise/channel robustness, on-device constraints, streaming-friendly encoders, and compute–latency trade-offs.
Use probes and metrics (ABX, phoneme classification, semantic similarity) to evaluate invariance and task readiness.
Discuss when to discretize encoder features versus using continuous vectors and implications for LM alignment.
Highlight modality gap issues (lexical tone, prosody, duration) and strategies to bridge them.

sections.section title: Token to Speech Decoding and Vocoders
sections.description: Explain rendering of predicted tokens back to waveform, covering decoders, vocoders, hybrid designs, and controls.

subsections.description: Compare codec decoders (Encodec/SoundStream), unit vocoders, and token-to-mel pipelines followed by neural vocoders.
Summarize GAN (HiFi-GAN), flow/diffusion, and AR/NAR decoders; loss functions for fidelity, prosody, and speaker identity.
Describe combining continuous vectors with semantic tokens to preserve timbre and reduce artifacts.
Cover prompt conditioning, speaker embeddings, residual vectors, and controls for emotion/prosody with latency considerations.

sections.description: Detail objectives, architectures, and adaptation strategies for modeling speech token sequences and mixed text–speech streams.

subsections.description: Contrast decoder-only AR, NAR, dual-token modeling, and flow-matching; interleaving speech/text streams.
Explain cold-start vs continued pretraining, modality projectors, and alignment losses for cross-modal transfer.
Discuss DualSpeechLM, FlowSLM, VecTokSpeech, Ichigo; handling mixed sequences and duplex interactions.
Summarize scaling trends, token-rate effects on perplexity and quality, and implications for capacity planning.

sections.description: Systematize multi-stage training and alignment, including synthetic supervision and diagnostics to avoid catastrophic forgetting.

subsections.description: Outline pretraining, modality adaptation, supervised fine-tuning, instruction tuning, and post-alignment (e.g., DPO).
Detail projectors, grounding, distillation, Stitch/KL alignment, and tokenizer→LM→decoder objective couplings.

subsections.subsection title: Synthetic and programmatic supervision at scale
subsections.description: Describe automatic pairing and scalable instruction datasets (LLaSO, LLaMA Omni-KE, Omni VoiceTextBlender, Slamming), with pros/cons.

subsections.subsection title: Modality alignment, sequence compression, and interface consistency
subsections.description: Explain maintaining consistent token interfaces and compressing sequences without eroding alignment.
Recommend practices to measure alignment quality, forgetting, and cross-modal retention with transparent reporting.

sections.description: Compare cascaded ASR→LLM→TTS and end-to-end SLMs, and categorize generation regimes and scheduling.

subsections.description: Contrast architectures by latency, controllability, and error propagation; include parallel and interleaved variants.
Cover hierarchical RVQ, flow/diffusion backbones, Groupformer, RQ-Transformer, and multi-token prediction for long horizons.
Define interleaving, parallel, and chunked generation; when to use each for different tasks.
Discuss joint semantic+acoustic generation, textless S2ST, and two-branch alignment/prediction systems.

sections.description: Survey modeling and control of prosody, identity, emotion, and social cues for expressive SLMs.

subsections.description: Review GOAT-SLM, ProsodyLM, SeamlessExpressiveLM and mechanisms capturing prosodic contours and speaker traits.
Explain word-level prosody tokens, multi-stream acoustic units, and unified tokens that preserve style cues.
Detail prompts, instructions, and token manipulations for style transfer, role-play, and editability.
Describe ALLM judges vs human raters for style, controllability metrics, and watermarking for edited segments (e.g., SSR Speech).

sections.section title: Real Time Streaming and Duplex Dialogue
sections.description: Address architectures and policies enabling low-latency streaming, full-duplex interaction, and natural turn-taking.

subsections.description: Explain chunking, buffering, low-bitrate tokenization, and budgeted inference for interactive agents.
Cover wait-k, read–write, incremental decoding, and their integration with tokenizers and SLMs.
Discuss barge-in, overlap handling, backchanneling, interruption detection, and conversational policy learning.
Describe streaming encoders and interleaved decoders (SALM Duplex, NTPP, SyncSpeech, Ichigo, Stitch) and real-time deployments.

sections.description: Catalog datasets, benchmark suites, and tasks, with guidance on protocols and multilingual/generalization dimensions.

subsections.description: List major corpora (LibriSpeech, LibriTTS, Common Voice, VoxPopuli, CoVoST2, VoxCeleb, GigaSpeech, AISHELL, Fisher, TELEVAL, CVSS-C) and categorize by modality, domain, and language.
Map tasks (ASR, TTS, S2ST, spoken QA, dialogue, style control, duplex) to datasets and standard protocols.
Survey SUPERB, VoxEval, ABX/sWUGGY/sBLIMP/sStoryCloze and capability-focused leaderboards.
Highlight datasets for low-resource, noisy, and streaming evaluation and domain shift considerations.
Discuss splits, contamination checks, licensing, and practices to ensure apples-to-apples comparisons.

sections.description: Define objective/subjective metrics and end-to-end protocols, emphasizing rate-aware and streaming/duplex evaluation.

subsections.subsection title: Metric taxonomy and selection by goal
subsections.description: Detail MOS, WER, BLEU/BERTScore, FAD, perplexity, codebook usage, bitrate, and reconstruction metrics and when to use them.
Specify evaluation setups for speech generation, streaming, and duplex dialogue with task-appropriate prompts and controls.
Design ablations on frame/token rates, semantic fidelity vs acoustic quality, and stability under compression.
Define real-time factor, time-to-first-token, streaming lag, and duplex overlap handling with standardized measurement.
Outline protocols for human/ALLM judges, inter-rater reliability, and significance testing.

sections.description: Analyze model/sequence efficiency, fast decoding, and deployment trade-offs for edge/server and duplex real-time systems.

subsections.description: Discuss reducing trainable parameters (LoRA/PEFT), partial finetuning, and strategies to avoid catastrophic forgetting.
Cover acoustic BPE, token-rate reduction, knowledge distillation, TinyWave, compact interleaved models, and sequence parallelization.
Present runtime strategies (multi-token prediction, speculative decoding, KV-caching) that reduce wall-clock latency.
Evaluate compute/memory/bandwidth under bitrate constraints, quantization, and MoE specialization for deployment.
Provide reproducible efficiency benchmarks and deployment patterns for real-time and duplex systems.

sections.description: Survey threat models, safeguards, privacy/fairness issues, and recommended reporting and red-teaming practices.

subsections.description: Detail jailbreaks, adversarial audio (e.g., SPIRIT), and non-spoken perturbations relevant to SLMs.
Propose data-time, training-time, decoding-time, and post-hoc safeguards; guardrails and watermarking (SSR Speech).
Discuss provenance tracking, anti-impersonation controls, consent, and privacy-preserving generation.
Examine augmentation-invariant discrete tokens and robustness across languages/dialects/speakers.
Address demographic performance disparities, evaluator bias, and data hygiene practices.
Recommend safety reporting, alignment documentation, and red-teaming protocols for speech agents.

sections.description: Review open ecosystems and offer a 5C framework to enable replicable research and fair comparison.

subsections.subsection title: 5C overview: Code, Config, Compute, Corpora, Comparison
subsections.description: Introduce the 5C lens for end-to-end reproducibility and benchmarking.
Highlight ESPnet, SpeechLM, LLaSO, OpenS2S, TinyWave, ComSL and end-to-end recipes.
Encourage standardized configs, reference components, and transparent pipelines.
Detail data curation, splitting, licensing, and contamination checks for apples-to-apples usage.
Promote open evaluation suites, metric protocols, and statistical testing for fair comparisons.
Provide guidance for reporting training hardware budgets and a consolidated resource table blueprint.

sections.description: Synthesize unresolved issues and promising directions for tokens, modeling, alignment, multilinguality, and safety.

subsections.subsection title: Unified vs multi-stream tokens and disentanglement
subsections.description: Debate universal tokens vs specialized streams and methods for semantic–acoustic disentanglement.
Identify needs for stable long-context reasoning and memory in duplex, real-world dialogue.
Outline transfer, data creation at scale, and robust cross-lingual performance goals.

subsections.subsection title: Alignment with text knowledge without forgetting
subsections.description: Propose training regimens that retain text LLM knowledge while acquiring speech skills.

subsections.subsection title: Toward a theory of rate vs capacity
subsections.description: Argue for principled study of token rate vs LM capacity, cross-layer abstraction alignment, and dual-channel modeling.
Summarize empirical design guidance and known limitations to inform future research.

sections.description: Recap the token taxonomy, modeling and system designs, training/alignment practices, and evaluation, with actionable recommendations.

subsections.description: Distill practical guidance on token interfaces, modeling choices, alignment, evaluation, and deployment.
Point to open toolkits, datasets, and call for standardized evaluations and open benchmarks.
